metadata.note: The Camden and Amboy Rail Road and Transportation Company (New Jersey, chartered 1830) and the same corridors after the Pennsylvania Railroad took over operation on Dec 1 1871: the original Bordentown - South Amboy main line, Camden - Bordentown, the Trenton Branch, the original canal-side Trenton - New Brunswick line, and the leased Camden & Burlington County (Camden - Mount Holly - Pemberton), Burlington & Mount Holly and Pemberton & Hightstown roads. One feature per span x operator; C&A features end 1871, PRR features on identical geometry begin 1871 (Rule 4 split at the lease). Research report: research/branches/camden_and_amboy_rail_road.txt.

metadata.operator_split: Dec 1 1871: every C&A line passes to PRR operation (lease of the United Companies, agreed June 30 1871); every C&A feature ends 1871 and a PRR feature on identical geometry starts 1871. The 1872 United New Jersey Railroad & Canal Co. consolidation did not change the operator. Feb 1 1968: the Pemberton Branch (the only line here still carrying passengers) passes to Penn Central - split into a Penn Central feature 1968-1969. Pemberton - Hightstown: PRR -> Union Transportation Co. in 1880 (Fowler) or 1888 (Wikipedia) - PRR drawn 1871-1880, Union Transportation 1888-1931, 1880-1888 undrawn. Burlington - Mount Holly: Burlington & Mount Holly Traction 1895-1901 (not drawn, see not_yet_sourced). The 1831 'Joint Companies' (with the Delaware & Raritan Canal) and the 1867 'United Companies' joint board were not operator changes.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Rule 5 trims applied at drawing time: Bordentown - Hightstown (opened Oct 1 1832) and Hightstown - South Amboy (Dec 17 1832) were horse-drawn until regular steam in September 1833, so the main line is drawn from 1833. The Philadelphia & Trenton's Morrisville - Trenton (State St) leg was horse-worked until 1844 (Fowler line 50) - not drawn here (the P&T is not in this layer), but septa.geojson's 1834-1871 Trenton Line segment covers it. The Camden & Burlington County's 1866 'Horse Car Railroad' never laid track; nothing to trim.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn (Rule 1). Excluded: Bordentown - Jamesburg after Oct 1938 (Robbinsville, Prospect Plains daggered freight-only in the 1952 Guide); Pemberton - Hightstown after 1931 (Union Transportation stations daggered); the Hightstown Industrial Track (Jamesburg - Cranbury, Conrail freight); the South Amboy coal dumpers (to 1971); Burlington - Mount Holly in its 1925 abandonment year; the Pemberton Branch after Apr 1969; the Kinkora Branch (no confirmed passenger year, see omitted).
omitted: [5] Trenton - New Brunswick NEW alignment via Princeton Junction, C&A 1864-1871: already drawn under NJ Transit (nj_transit_rail.geojson njt-10, segment 1863-1871) and as part of the PRR NEC (pennsylvania_railroad.geojson); a C&A feature here would double-draw the corridor.
[6] Princeton Branch, C&A 1865-1871: already drawn under NJ Transit (nj_transit_rail.geojson njt-15, segment 1865-1871); not double-drawn.
[7] Philadelphia & Trenton, C&A-operated 1836-1871: already drawn under SEPTA (septa.geojson septa-TRE, segment 1834-1871); not double-drawn.
[11] Kingston Branch / Rocky Hill RR, C&A era: operator for 1864-1871 not established and opening date in three-way conflict (1864 / 1866 / 1870) - drawable NONE.

[18] PRR Rocky Hill (Kingston) Branch, Monmouth Junction - Rocky Hill, 1872 [OPEN] - 1875 [OPEN]: the 1872 evidence is a Princetonian search snippet only and the operator/lessee status is unchecked; omitted per the tracing instruction.

Kinkora Branch (Kinkora - Columbus - Jobstown - Juliustown - Pemberton - Birmingham, Columbus, Kinkora & Springfield RR, 1872): no confirmed passenger year (1952 Guide Table 37 times not recoverable, two stations daggered); not proof it never had passengers.
Burlington & Mount Holly Traction Co. electric operation of Burlington - Mount Holly, 1895-1901: omitted operator era, see not_yet_sourced.
Pemberton - Hightstown 1880-1888: operator disputed (PRR vs Union Transportation), left undrawn.
not_yet_sourced: RULE 4 SPLITS NEEDED IN OTHER LAYERS (not made here, those files were not touched): nj_transit_rail.geojson njt-10 (Northeast Corridor) draws Trenton - New Brunswick 1863/1864-1871 in NJ Transit colour although the Camden and Amboy ran it, and 1871-1968 although the PRR ran it; njt-15 (Princeton Shuttle) likewise for 1865-1871 (C&A) and 1871-1968 (PRR); septa.geojson septa-TRE (Trenton Line) draws 1834-1871 in SEPTA colour although the C&A operated the Philadelphia & Trenton from 1836, and its Morrisville - Trenton leg was horse-worked to 1844 (Rule 5, Fowler only); pennsylvania_railroad.geojson's NEC feature draws PRR company/colour in New Jersey for 1838-1871, when the PRR ran nothing there (C&A Trenton - New Brunswick, NJRR&T New Brunswick - Jersey City), on the post-1863 / post-1910 alignment. When those are split, the C&A-era pieces should take this layer's Camden and Amboy colour.
Trenton - New Brunswick realignment: Nov 23 1863 (nj_transit_rail.geojson note, no source given) vs 'Closed 1864' (Fowler line 55). The canal line is drawn to 1863.

Pemberton & Hightstown: opening Feb 1867 (Rutgers finding aid) vs 1868 (Wikipedia) vs fully complete 1869 - drawn from 1869. PRR -> Union Transportation in 1880 (Fowler) vs July 31 1888 (Wikipedia) - 1880-1888 undrawn. Passenger end 1931 is UNCITED in Wikipedia and otherwise rests only on Fowler's '1880>1931'; needs an ICC finance docket or a 1931 newspaper. Treat 1931 as the last claimed year, not a confirmed end.

Burlington - Mount Holly: OMITTED OPERATOR ERA - Fowler says the line was worked electrically by the Burlington & Mount Holly Traction Co. 1895>1901 (an interurban over the PRR rails, per Fowler's wording, not checked further); not drawn. Whether PRR steam trains ran alongside the trolley 1895-1901 is unknown. The 1924 PRR passenger end rests on Fowler alone (Wikipedia gives only the 1925 abandonment).
Burlington & Mount Holly 1849-1867 and Burlington & Mount Holly's Mount Holly - Pemberton section 1863-1867: operator and motive power not established; undrawn.
Exact first steam day on the C&A main line: Sept 9 vs Sept 19 1833; whether any horse working was retained after 1833 was not checked.
PRR-era end dates 1938, 1959, 1963 and 1969 were read through Wikipedia's citations of dated newspapers (Home News 1938/1959, Courier-Post 1963/1969); the newspapers were not read.

South Amboy (1st) waterfront terminal: last passenger use and the end of the Amboy steamboat connection are not dated; by 1951 the Jamesburg trains used South Amboy Junction / Perth Amboy. The Jamesburg - South Amboy PRR feature is drawn to the waterfront for its whole span.
Wikipedia's Camden and Amboy summary says '1832: Trenton-New Brunswick service began' and also 'Trenton to New Brunswick (1839)'; 1839 (matching Fowler) is used.
Gauge: the C&A was 4 ft 10 in gauge, converted 1872-1905 (Fowler) - no effect on drawn years.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh on every feature are estimates; no timetable frequency or running time was counted.
Freehold & Jamesburg Agricultural RR (1853; C&A subscribed stock) - not established that the C&A ran its trains; separate research queue entry, not drawn here.

properties.line: Camden and Amboy: Bordentown – South Amboy
properties.speed_source: estimate, not sourced: no running time was checked for any year; a figure typical of a mid-19th-century (C&A era) or early-20th-century (PRR era) local passenger train in flat country
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap (ODbL), Overpass (overpass-api.openhistoricalmap.org): ways -201857311, -201857315, -201858593, -201857314, -201858767, -201858777, -201858528 (dated C&A main line). Routed with opstrace.py (OHM ways dated <=1871 preferred over modern track); Douglas-Peucker 8 m + trim_reversals. OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror): ways tagged old_railway_operator=PRR (Amboy Secondary, Browns #1 Running Track, Jamesburg Wye), checked against OpenHistoricalMap way -201858528. Routed with opstrace.py; Douglas-Peucker 8 m + trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Bordentown junction - Jamesburg: 20.5 mi traced against 21.5 mi documented (Fowler NJ line 61, Fieldsboro 27.0 - Jamesburg 48.5; Fowler's datum is at Fieldsboro on the Camden line, the drawn line starts at the Bordentown junction a little north of it). Real-traced throughout on OpenHistoricalMap ways dated to the C&A openings (start_date 1832-10 Bordentown - Windsor - Hightstown, 1832-12 Hightstown - Jamesburg, sourced in OHM to Coverdale & Colpitts); no approximated (straight-line) legs. OpenHistoricalMap ways are hand-drawn at coarser resolution than OSM track; checked against OSM railway / abandoned / old_railway_operator=PRR ways where both exist: median offset 40 m, 90th percentile 190 m. The lifted Windsor - Hightstown - Prospect Plains stretch also matches OSM's razed/abandoned ways tagged old_railway_operator=PRR 'Main Line (Camden to Amboy)'. Era: the OHM ways are the 1832 alignment; no later relocation is known. Jamesburg - South Amboy: 12.7 mi drawn against 12.5 mi documented (Fowler NJ line 61, Jamesburg 48.5 - South Amboy Jct 61.0; about 34 mi for the whole Bordentown - South Amboy line, 33.2 mi drawn). Real-traced on today's OSM track tagged old_railway_operator=PRR (Amboy Secondary 10.7 mi, Browns #1 Running Track 2.0 mi, Jamesburg Wye / Freehold Secondary 0.3 mi); APPROXIMATED: one straight link of 0.25 mi (398 m) at Jamesburg joining the end of the OHM-traced Bordentown - Jamesburg line to the OSM track; otherwise no approximated legs. Checked against OpenHistoricalMap's dated C&A way (start_date 1832-12) over the same stretch: every OHM vertex lies within 250 m of the drawn line and the drawn line follows it to OHM's terminal point at the South Amboy waterfront, so the modern freight track is taken to be on the original alignment. The exact position of the 1830s-1870s South Amboy steamboat wharf was not verified.

segments.note: The original Camden and Amboy main line and the New York - Philadelphia rail-and-steamboat route: steamboat New York - South Amboy (waterfront), rail via Yardville, Robbinsville (Newtown), Windsor (Centreville), Hightstown, Cranbury (Station), Prospect Plains, Jamesburg, Spotswood and Old Bridge to Bordentown, then boat (to 1834) or rail (from 1834) to Camden. Bordentown - Hightstown opened Oct 1 1832 and Hightstown - South Amboy Dec 17 1832, both HORSE-DRAWN; regular steam (the John Bull) from September 1833 (Sept 9 or Sept 19 - sources differ), so the drawn span starts 1833 (Rule 5). Through New York traffic moved to the Trenton - New Brunswick line from 1839, but this line kept local and Amboy-boat service through 1871. The Camden and Amboy's lines passed to Pennsylvania Railroad operation on Dec 1 1871 (lease of the United Companies agreed June 30 1871), so this C&A feature ends in 1871 and the PRR feature on the same geometry begins there. headway_min is an estimate (no timetable frequency was counted for this span).
sources: Segment-level: openings Oct 1 / Dec 17 1832 (horse) from the Wikipedia Amboy Branch article (citing Coverdale & Colpitts 1946); steam from Sept 1833 from the John Bull and Hightstown rail accident articles; 1851 stations (Bordentown Shops, Centreville, Cranberry Station, Jamesburg) from Fowler NJ line 61, letter x; 1871 end = PRR lease, Philadelphia & Trenton article

properties.geometry_quality: Camden - Bordentown junction: 25.9 mi traced against 27.1 mi documented (Fowler NJ line 60, Camden 1.0 - Bordentown 28.1). Real-traced on the OpenHistoricalMap way dated start_date 1834-09 (Coverdale & Colpitts), 25.3 mi, plus 0.1 mi of OSM River Line track, finished along OHM ways -201857312/-201857313/-201857330 (1834-09) into Bordentown station where the 1832 line begins; no approximated legs. OpenHistoricalMap ways are hand-drawn at coarser resolution than OSM track; checked against OSM railway / abandoned / old_railway_operator=PRR ways where both exist: median offset 34 m, 90th percentile 135 m. The line starts at OHM's Camden end of the 1834 way (in Camden, roughly 1 mi inland of the Delaware River ferry slips; Fowler's Camden milepost is 1.0); the final approach to the ferry is not drawn because no dated way for it exists. Today's NJ Transit River Line light rail (OSM, old_railway_operator=PRR) runs on this corridor and was checked as a stand-in, but the dated OHM way was preferred; the River Line is not drawn as such.

segments.note: Camden (Federal Street ferry, for Philadelphia) - Palmyra - Riverton - Riverside - Beverly - Burlington - Florence - Kinkora - Fieldsboro - Bordentown, opened September 1834 (Coverdale & Colpitts p.67), completing the all-rail Camden - South Amboy line. Locomotive-operated: the C&A had used steam since Sept 1833 and no source says this section opened with horses. Burlington is the junction for the Mount Holly line. The Camden and Amboy's lines passed to Pennsylvania Railroad operation on Dec 1 1871 (lease of the United Companies agreed June 30 1871), so this C&A feature ends in 1871 and the PRR feature on the same geometry begins there. headway_min is an estimate (no timetable frequency was counted for this span).

properties.line: Camden and Amboy: Trenton – New Brunswick (canal line)
properties.speed_source: estimate, not sourced: no running time was checked for any year; a figure typical of a mid-19th-century (C&A era) or early-20th-century (PRR era) local passenger train in flat country
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap (ODbL): ways -201857128, -201857125 (1839-1863 canal grade), -201857129 (1839-1976), -201857130 (1839, Monmouth Junction - New Brunswick). Routed with opstrace.py; Douglas-Peucker 8 m + trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Trenton (State Street) - New Brunswick, ORIGINAL canal line: 26.6 mi traced against about 26 mi documented (Fowler NJ line 55 Trenton 59 - Kingston 44, line 50 Deans 39.9 - New Brunswick 32.7; not measured precisely). Real-traced on OpenHistoricalMap ways: start_date 1839-01-01 / end_date 1863 for the canal-side grade Trenton - Clarksville - Princeton canal basin - Kingston (12.1 mi; it lies beside the Delaware & Raritan Canal towpath, part of which OSM tags old_railway_operator=PRR), 1839-01-01 - 1976 for Kingston - Monmouth Junction (4.7 mi, the later Kingston / Rocky Hill branch), and 1839-01-01 for Trenton and for Monmouth Junction - Deans - New Brunswick (9.5 mi); no approximated legs. OpenHistoricalMap ways are hand-drawn at coarser resolution than OSM track; checked against OSM railway / abandoned / old_railway_operator=PRR ways where both exist: median offset 43 m, 90th percentile 466 m. (the larger offsets are on the lifted canal-side grade, where OSM has little to compare with). RULE 2 ERA STATEMENT: this is the pre-1864 alignment, NOT today's Northeast Corridor via Princeton Junction, for Trenton - Monmouth Junction; Monmouth Junction - Deans - New Brunswick is shared with the later main line and is drawn on its mapped (current) geometry, so any post-1863 widening or easing of curves there is drawn as it now is.

segments.note: The ORIGINAL Trenton - New Brunswick line, the first Philadelphia - New York Harbor rail link: Trenton (State Street) - Clarksville - Princeton (C&A station at the Delaware & Raritan Canal basin) - Aqueduct Turnout - Kingston - Monmouth Junction - Deans - New Brunswick, laid along the canal bank as far as Kingston; through New York trains connected at New Brunswick with the New Jersey Rail Road & Transportation Co. (a separate company, not drawn here). Opened 1839 (Wikipedia; Fowler: Trenton State St 1839>1863). Replaced by the new alignment via Princeton Junction: the nj_transit_rail.geojson note gives Nov 23 1863, Fowler line 55 says 'Closed 1864' - sources differ by up to a year, and the drawn end is the earlier, 1863. Fowler lists Princeton (C&A) and Aqueduct Turnout in 1851 (x). The Monmouth Junction - Kingston piece survived as the Kingston / Rocky Hill branch, not drawn (operator and dates open). headway_min is an estimate (no timetable frequency was counted for this span).
sources: Segment-level: 1839 opening from the Wikipedia Camden and Amboy article; 1839>1863 and the 1851 stations from Fowler NJ lines 50 and 55; end 1863 (Nov 23 1863 per the unsourced nj_transit_rail.geojson note) vs 1864 (Fowler 'Closed 1864') recorded as a conflict, earlier year drawn

properties.line: Camden and Amboy: Camden – Pemberton (via Mount Holly)
properties.speed_source: estimate, not sourced: no running time was checked for any year; a figure typical of a mid-19th-century (C&A era) or early-20th-century (PRR era) local passenger train in flat country
properties.geometry_source: OpenHistoricalMap (ODbL): ways -201889157, -201889158, -201889159 (start_date 1867-10-21), -201888734, -201888754, -201888755 (start_date 1863-07-04) and short Mount Holly pieces. Routed with opstrace.py (PRSL- and Reading-tagged ways excluded); Douglas-Peucker 8 m + trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Pavonia (Camden) - Pemberton: 22.4 mi traced against 22.4 mi documented (Fowler NJ line 66, Pavonia 3.4 - South Pemberton 25.8). Real-traced on OpenHistoricalMap ways dated start_date 1867-10-21 (Pavonia - Mount Holly, the C&BC extension) and 1863-07-04 (Mount Holly - Pemberton, the Burlington & Mount Holly extension); no approximated legs. OpenHistoricalMap ways are hand-drawn at coarser resolution than OSM track; checked against OSM railway / abandoned / old_railway_operator=PRR ways where both exist: median offset 42 m, 90th percentile 190 m. Starts at the Pavonia junction with the Camden - Bordentown main line (trains ran on into Camden over that line, drawn in the Camden - Bordentown features, not repeated here). Ends at the end of OHM's 1863 way at the junction with the Pemberton & Hightstown, Pemberton (about 0.8 km from the borough centre; whether the 1860s Pemberton station stood exactly there was not checked). The ex-PRSL / PATCO and Reading (Atlantic City RR) lines around Camden were excluded from routing; the drawn line uses none of them.

segments.note: The Camden & Burlington County Railroad, Camden (Pavonia, junction with the Camden - Bordentown main line, over which trains ran on into Camden) - Merchantville - Maple Shade - Moorestown - Hartford - Masonville - Hainesport - Mount Holly - Smithville - Birmingham - Pemberton. The Mount Holly - Pavonia extension was completed Oct 21 1867 and 'the Camden and Amboy then leased' the C&BC (Coverdale & Colpitts pp.221-222). The Mount Holly - Pemberton part had opened Jan 1 1863 under the Burlington & Mount Holly, but who worked it before 1867 is not established, so nothing earlier is drawn. The 'Horse Car Railroad' merged into the C&BC in 1866 never laid track, so no Rule 5 trim is needed. The Camden and Amboy's lines passed to Pennsylvania Railroad operation on Dec 1 1871 (lease of the United Companies agreed June 30 1871), so this C&A feature ends in 1871 and the PRR feature on the same geometry begins there. headway_min is an estimate (no timetable frequency was counted for this span).
sources: Segment-level: Oct 21 1867 completion and C&A lease from the Wikipedia Pemberton Branch and Camden and Burlington County Railroad articles (citing Coverdale & Colpitts pp.221-222); 1871 end = PRR lease
